# 📝 NCM 119: Quick Notes & High-Yield Examination Cheat Sheet
## Nursing Care Delivery Systems (Modalities of Care)

> **Course**: Nursing Care Management 119 (NCM 119) — Nursing Leadership & Management  
> **Target Audience**: 4th Year Nursing Students (Philippine Nursing Licensure Examination [PNLE] & NCLEX-RN Candidates)  
> **Rule Applied**: All abbreviations and acronyms are 100% expanded for complete clarity.

---

## 🎯 Master Modality Comparison Matrix

Use this high-yield matrix to answer 80% of board exam questions on care delivery models instantly.

| Care Delivery Modality | Pioneer / Historical Era | Key Authority & Structure | Accountability Span | Continuity of Care | Cost & Staffing Mix | Hallmark Clinical Setting | Chief Advantage | Critical Pitfall / Weakness |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Case Method / Total Patient Care (TPC)** | Florence Nightingale (19th Century); 1920s Private Duty | Direct 1:1 or 1:2; Registered Nurse (RN) provides **all** aspects of care for assigned client(s) | **Shift-Only** (8 to 12 hours) | High for the shift; low across shifts if nurses rotate | **High Cost**; requires 100% Registered Nurses (RN) | Intensive Care Unit (ICU), Post-Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU), Labor and Delivery (L&D) | Holistic, unfragmented care; immediate response to acute changes | Very costly; inefficient for non-critical, stable patients |
| **Functional Nursing** | 1930s Great Depression & World War II (Severe RN shortages) | Charge Nurse assigns **tasks** rather than patients (Medication Nurse, Treatment Nurse, Vital Signs Aide) | **Task-Only** (No single nurse owns whole patient care) | **Lowest** (Severe fragmentation; patient sees many nurses) | **Lowest Cost**; high utilization of Licensed Practical Nurses (LPN) & Unlicensed Assistive Personnel (UAP) | Disasters, emergency field hospitals, mass vaccination drives | Extreme efficiency, high task proficiency, economical | Fragmented care, missed subtle holistic changes, depersonalization |
| **Team Nursing** | Eleanor Lambertsen (1950s) | Registered Nurse (RN) **Team Leader** directs team members (RNs, LPNs, UAPs) for a group of patients | **Shift-Only** via Team Leader supervision | Moderate; dependent on clear team communication | **Moderate Cost**; balanced mix of professionals and assistive personnel | Acute Medical-Surgical units, Step-Down Telemetry wards | Maximizes diverse skills; fosters team collaboration and democratic input | Failed if Team Leader has poor communication or skips conferences |
| **Modular Nursing** | Magargal (1980s / 1990s) | Geographic adaptation of Team Nursing; unit split into physical zones/pods with fixed mini-teams | **Shift-Only** within designated geographic module | Moderate to High; consistent mini-team per physical pod | **Moderate Cost**; efficient spatial staffing | Large hospital wings, long surgical corridors, decentralized units | Eliminates wasted transit/walking time; supplies kept at bedside | Requires architectural support (pod-based architectural layout) |
| **Primary Nursing** | Marie Manthey (Late 1960s / 1970s) | One **Primary Nurse (RN)** designs 24-hour care plan from admission to discharge; **Associate Nurses** execute during off-shifts | **24 Hours / Day (Admission to Discharge)** | **Highest**; single accountable clinician coordinates entire stay | **High Cost**; requires predominantly all-RN staff mix | Oncology units, Pediatric wards, Hospice, Primary rehabilitation | Unmatched clinical autonomy, continuity, and patient satisfaction | Expensive; high stress on Primary Nurse; broken if Associate Nurse alters plan |
| **Case Management** | 1980s Managed Care Era (Health Maintenance Organizations [HMO]) | **Nurse Case Manager** coordinates care across health continuum (inpatient, outpatient, post-acute) | **Entire Episode of Illness** (Across health settings) | **Comprehensive Longitudinal Continuity** | **Cost-Effective Systemic Model**; prevents readmission | High-risk chronic diseases (Heart Failure, Diabetes), Rehabilitation | Prevents hospital readmissions; slashes length of stay; controls costs | Does not provide direct bedside hands-on physical care |
| **Critical Pathways (Care Maps)** | 1980s New England Medical Center | Multidisciplinary timeline grid matching interventions to specific recovery milestones by day/hour | **Protocol-Driven** across clinical trajectory | Standardized, predictable clinical progression | Reduces length of stay (LOS) and financial variances under DRGs | Predictable clinical conditions (Total Knee Replacement, Uncomplicated AMI) | Eliminates practice variation; establishes clear discharge benchmarks | Inflexible for multimorbid patients; requires active variance tracking |

## 🔑 Board Exam "Trigger Word" Recognition Guide

When analyzing clinical scenario exam stems, search for these exact buzzwords to identify the correct modality:

* 🚨 **"24-hour total accountability from admission to discharge"** $\rightarrow$ **Primary Nursing**
* 🚨 **"Associate nurse provides care following the care plan on off-shifts"** $\rightarrow$ **Primary Nursing**
* 🚨 **"Oldest method of care delivery"** OR **"Private-duty nursing model"** $\rightarrow$ **Case Method / Total Patient Care (TPC)**
* 🚨 **"One Registered Nurse provides all hygienic, physical, and pharmacological care during the shift"** $\rightarrow$ **Case Method / Total Patient Care (TPC)**
* 🚨 **"Task-oriented"** OR **"One nurse gives injections, one nurse takes vital signs, one does dressings"** $\rightarrow$ **Functional Nursing**
* 🚨 **"Division of labor during acute wartime / nurse shortage"** $\rightarrow$ **Functional Nursing**
* 🚨 **"Pre-shift and post-shift team conferences"** $\rightarrow$ **Team Nursing**
* 🚨 **"Team Leader assigns tasks based on scope of practice and staff qualifications"** $\rightarrow$ **Team Nursing**
* 🚨 **"Geographic assignment"** OR **"Decentralized patient modules to reduce nurse walking time"** $\rightarrow$ **Modular Nursing**
* 🚨 **"Coordinates care across an entire episode of illness from pre-admission to post-discharge"** $\rightarrow$ **Case Management**
* 🚨 **"Multidisciplinary care map tracking positive and negative variances"** $\rightarrow$ **Critical Pathways**
* 🚨 **"Ida Jean Orlando (1958)"** $\rightarrow$ **Deliberative Nursing Process (ADPIE) & dynamic nurse-patient relationship**
* 🚨 **"Patient Classification System (PCS)"** $\rightarrow$ **Acuity-based workload measurement for equitable, safe staffing ratios**

## 🧠 High-Yield Memory Mnemonics

### 1. The 5 Steps of the Nursing Process: **ADPIE**
* **A** — **Assessment**: Systematic collection of subjective and objective client health data.
* **D** — **Diagnosis**: Formulating clinical judgment about human responses to health conditions (NANDA-I).
* **P** — **Planning**: Establishing measurable patient-centered goals, priorities, and expected outcomes.
* **I** — **Implementation**: Executing evidence-based clinical interventions and direct care.
* **E** — **Evaluation**: Assessing client progress against established outcome criteria and revising care.

### 2. Functional Nursing: **FAST**
* **F** — **Fragmented** care (client sees multiple staff members for different tasks).
* **A** — **Assembly-line** task efficiency (medication nurse, treatment nurse, hygiene aide).
* **S** — **Shortage** response (designed for severe RN deficits during wartime and disasters).
* **T** — **Task-centered** rather than patient-centered.

### 3. Team Nursing: **TEAM**
* **T** — **Together** (RN, LPN, and UAP collaborate under shared care goals).
* **E** — **Eleanor Lambertsen** (developed the framework in the 1950s).
* **A** — **Allocated** tasks based on individual competencies and licensure scopes.
* **M** — **Morning / Post-Shift Conferences** (mandatory communication sessions led by the Team Leader).

### 4. Primary Nursing: **PRIME**
* **P** — **Permanent** 24-hour accountability from admission to discharge.
* **R** — **Registered Nurse (RN)** driven (all-RN staffing philosophy developed by Marie Manthey).
* **I** — **Individualized** comprehensive nursing care plan formulated by one primary nurse.
* **M** — **Manthey, Marie** (the visionary founder).
* **E** — **Execution** by Associate Nurses during the Primary Nurse's off-duty hours.

### 5. Patient Classification System (PCS) Acuity Classes: **I to IV**
* **Category I (Minimal Care / Self-Care)**: Clinically stable; independent in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs); 1–2 hours nursing care/day.
* **Category II (Moderate Care / Intermediate)**: Partially dependent in ADLs; periodic medication administration and vital signs; 3–5 hours nursing care/day.
* **Category III (Acute Care / Maximum)**: Bedbound; heavily dependent in ADLs; complex wound dressings, intravenous medications; 6–9 hours nursing care/day.
* **Category IV (Critical Care / Intensive)**: Hemodynamically unstable; life-support equipment; hourly or continuous titration; 12–24 hours nursing care/day (1:1 or 1:2 nurse-to-patient ratio).

## 📊 Patient Classification System (PCS) Quick Reference

```
                [PATIENT CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (PCS)]
                                  │
      ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
      ▼                                                       ▼
[FACTOR EVALUATION SYSTEM]                             [PROTOTYPE EVALUATION SYSTEM]
- Evaluates discrete clinical tasks                    - Evaluates broad patient diagnostic profile
- Sums point values (e.g., Foley = 15 pts,             - Groups into broad descriptive categories
  IVPB = 10 pts, Trach suctioning = 20 pts)             (e.g., "Standard Post-Op Day 1 Patient")
- High objective precision                             - Fast and efficient; less granular
```

### Purpose of Patient Classification System (PCS):
1. **Determines Safe Staffing Numbers and Skill Mix** (Matches RN, LPN, UAP ratios to patient acuity).
2. **Budgeting & Fiscal Justification** (Provides data to defend nursing staff budgets to hospital boards).
3. **Workload Equity** (Prevents nurse burnout by distributing high-acuity patients evenly across staff).
4. **Safety & Quality Compliance** (Meets regulatory accreditation standards for hospital licensing).
